buddhism_sutras_part_31_20.meaning: We must let go of distractions to find peace and presence in our current moment.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_20.context: Children are left alone in a room, symbolizing a shift in focus and attention.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_21.meaning: Stay focused on your spiritual goals and do not get distracted by temporary worldly desires.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_21.context: A humorous warning about staying on the right path unless you have a good reason.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_22.meaning: Your inner self is more precious than any external scenery, so nurture your soul with care.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_22.context: A comparison between the beauty of nature and the inner beauty of the human spirit.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_23.meaning: Seeking validation from those who do not value you only leads to suffering and emptiness.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_23.context: A person begs for love from someone who does not care, showing deep emotional pain.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_24.meaning: Your persistent thoughts shape your reality, so choose positive and constructive ideas to attract good outcomes.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_24.context: Repeating thoughts to yourself creates a mental pattern that eventually shapes your reality.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_25.meaning: You have the power to find meaning in life by responding creatively to its big questions.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_25.context: Humans have the unique power to creatively engage with the mystery of why we exist.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_26.meaning: Appreciate the good in the past but work hard today to create a better tomorrow.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_26.context: Acknowledging the past while encouraging effort to improve the future through hard work.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_35.meaning: You must release your attachments to find inner calm. Holding on to worldly desires only blocks your path to lasting happiness.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_35.context: The Buddha teaches that letting go of bad habits leads to true peace and spiritual freedom for everyone.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_36.meaning: We must protect and share sacred knowledge. This ensures that wisdom survives and helps people find truth in later times.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_36.context: The community preserves ancient teachings so future generations can learn about the Buddha and his wise guidance.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_37.meaning: You cannot escape the results of your actions. Every deed has a consequence that will eventually catch up with you.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_37.context: No place on earth or in nature can hide you from the consequences of your bad choices.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_38.meaning: True greatness comes from wisdom and kindness. We should honor those who think deeply and act with moral integrity.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_38.context: A speaker praises another person for their noble character, deep thought, and great understanding of life.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_39.meaning: It is unjust to punish the innocent for others sins. We should seek fairness and not blame the wrong people.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_39.context: David feels it is unfair that he suffers for the mistakes made by another person named Nancy.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_40.meaning: Angry arguments often lead to confusion. Clear communication is better than shouting nonsense that no one can understand.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_40.context: Two men argue loudly with confusing words, showing how messy and unclear their disagreement has become.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_41.meaning: A divine calling brings deep inner peace. Trusting your purpose to help others can calm your troubled mind.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_41.context: A vision promises that Siddhattha will become a Buddha and save humanity, filling his heart with peace.

buddhism_sutras_part_31_42.meaning: People often make decisions based on money. Greed can blind us to the true value or character of others.
buddhism_sutras_part_31_42.context: A musician tells a boss that a painter will pay, and the boss agrees because he sees money.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_37.meaning: Life is very short and fragile so we should not waste our precious time on things that do not matter.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_37.context: Death comes quickly and takes lives away just like farmers cut down tall green grass in a field.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_38.meaning: It is enough to keep your inner peace and protect your spirit from stress and worry during difficult times.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_38.context: We often want more things or try to be better but in hard times we must focus on staying calm.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_39.meaning: We must set clear boundaries and remove toxic people from our lives to protect our own peace and happiness.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_39.context: A woman named la Sanginne was tired of bad behavior and told her partner she would leave if he stayed.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_40.meaning: Life works best when we follow its natural rhythm instead of forcing outcomes or trying to control every single moment.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_40.context: Breathing is vital for life but trying to control it too much causes problems and stops the natural flow.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_41.meaning: True freedom comes from knowing what to keep and what to let go of so we can live with less burden.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_41.context: We receive many gifts and experiences in life but we must choose which ones help us grow and which ones hurt.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_42.meaning: Spiritual practice is not about becoming someone else but about discovering and embracing your true unique self without hiding.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_42.context: The speaker realized that meditation does not change people into a new type but helps them become more themselves.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_43.meaning: Simple acts of kindness and joy can deeply touch our hearts and remind us of the beauty in living.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_43.context: A beautiful smile from another person brings great joy and makes the heart feel full of life and happiness.

buddhism_sutras_part_33_44.meaning: Real growth needs consistent effort and sincere commitment because quick fixes do not work for deep inner change and peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_33_44.context: Walking the spiritual path requires serious effort and honest dedication to keep going without giving up or stopping.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_20.meaning: Your inner peace shows on your face. Choose joy over sadness to live a better life.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_20.context: One person looks happy and young while another looks sad and stuck in dark thoughts.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_21.meaning: Do not add more stress to your life. Find peace by letting go of unnecessary worries.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_21.context: The speaker prefers to clear away confusing thoughts rather than creating new problems or worries.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_22.meaning: Forced actions feel empty. True devotion comes from the heart, not from being pushed by others.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_22.context: A person is forced to pray many times when they really wanted to do something else instead.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_23.meaning: Family ties are strong. We should always be ready to face our loved ones with honesty.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_23.context: A man grabs his friend and points out his family arriving to look for him urgently.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_24.meaning: Share comfort with those who suffer. Kind words and gifts help heal a broken heart.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_24.context: A man offers wine to comfort a friend who has lost everything and feels very sad.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_25.meaning: Simple meals can be satisfying. Appreciate what you have instead of wanting fancy or expensive food.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_25.context: The innkeeper serves a large dish of meat bones swimming in a rich and tasty sauce.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_26.meaning: Let your mind be free like the sky. Connect with nature to find true inner peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_26.context: The speaker feels their mind flying high with seagulls over the vast and open ocean.

buddhism_sutras_part_41_27.meaning: Good actions shape your future. Live kindly now so you leave a positive mark on the world.
buddhism_sutras_part_41_27.context: A holy man gave gifts and did good deeds before he died and moved on.

buddhism_sutras_part_45_49.meaning: Joy often shows up when we stop looking for it and simply live in the moment.
buddhism_sutras_part_45_49.context: A Buddhist teaching that happiness can appear unexpectedly, not only from chasing goals.

buddhism_sutras_part_45_50.meaning: Life is full of busy, noisy distractions that can surround us without meaning.
buddhism_sutras_part_45_50.context: Describes animals and a noisy flock moving around a person in a shallow pool.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_1.meaning: Even after long practice, one remains part of the spiritual family and its teachings.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_1.context: The speaker says they still belong to the Buddhist community after many years.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_2.meaning: Everything depends on other things and is not truly separate or permanent.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_2.context: Explains that things arise together and have no fixed, independent existence.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_3.meaning: She wants help with a simple task, showing trust and the value of community support.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_3.context: A woman asks someone to visit a farm to learn about butter, a popular place for kids.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_4.meaning: Our true nature stays the same even while we experience constant change.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_4.context: States that the unchanging self appears as changing in everyday life.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_5.meaning: Even powerful beings seek wisdom, and the Buddha provides insight into true sharpness.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_5.context: A deity asks the Buddha about the sharpest sword, and the Buddha answers.

buddhism_sutras_part_46_6.meaning: The act shows renewal and the importance of naming and blessing in spiritual growth.
buddhism_sutras_part_46_6.context: A dean gives salt and water to a man named Thylbert, symbolizing abundance, and baptizes him again.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_32.meaning: Greed and complaints often come from a place of fear, not true need or happiness.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_32.context: A merchant complains about high prices while asking a group of women to confirm his claim.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_33.meaning: Without wisdom and skill, our efforts often miss the mark and fail to help us.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_33.context: Poor people try to shoot arrows but miss their target because they lack proper training.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_34.meaning: Opening your heart to love lets you see reality clearly and live with more peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_34.context: Practicing loving kindness helps us see life clearly and change how we relate to it.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_35.meaning: True freedom means stopping the search and resting in the peace you already have.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_35.context: The final stage of spiritual growth is realizing there is no more path to walk.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_36.meaning: How you treat your parents today teaches your children how to treat you later.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_36.context: A wise teacher advises that caring for elders sets a good example for your kids.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_37.meaning: Stop searching far away for happiness, because the answer is already inside your own mind.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_37.context: People often look outside for answers, but looking inside is actually the easier way.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_38.meaning: Life is full of unexpected events, so we must stay calm and observe what happens.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_38.context: A traveler rests in a grove where thirty friends are having a party and losing items.

buddhism_sutras_part_51_39.meaning: You cannot defeat everyone else, but you can win by calming your own angry heart.
buddhism_sutras_part_51_39.context: A warrior realizes that fighting others never ends, but calming anger stops the real war.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_7.meaning: Sharing ancient wisdom with new people helps spread understanding and keeps old teachings alive.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_7.context: A governor and Buddhist scholar worked together to translate old Buddha stories into English.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_8.meaning: When you know your true self, you do not need outside things to feel happy or whole.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_8.context: A teacher explains how finding your inner light helps you stop pretending to be someone else.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_9.meaning: Accept that good and bad things happen, and trust that the universe balances everything out.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_9.context: A simple saying reminds us that life has both good times and bad times for everyone.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_10.meaning: Sometimes we must do boring duties, even when we would rather do something we love.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_10.context: A character named Nancy is annoyed because she must care for a pig instead of painting.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_11.meaning: When we see people clearly, we realize everyone is just trying their best in life.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_11.context: A speaker talks about how seeing clearly helps us treat all people with equal respect.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_12.meaning: Unexpected events can appear suddenly, reminding us that life is full of strange surprises.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_12.context: A dark figure suddenly appears from a fire pile and sits next to the narrator on a tower.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_13.meaning: Stories can make ordinary people seem like heroes, and children often believe what they hear.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_13.context: A woman tells exciting stories about a man's horse skills, and the children believe every word.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_14.meaning: Sometimes we must search for special people or things to solve big problems in our world.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_14.context: Two characters discuss a quest to find seven people who will save their land from trouble.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_33.meaning: The low cough indicates a hidden presence, reminding us to pay attention to those who may be in need or suffering. The conversation highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_33.context: A cough is heard in a quiet setting, and two characters, a master and an unknown person, are discussing.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_34.meaning: The hospitaller shows interest in Ulenspiegel's skills and the importance of sharing knowledge and helping others.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_34.context: A hospitaller meets Ulenspiegel and inquires about his healing abilities.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_35.meaning: Understanding the transient nature of life and accepting our circumstances leads to inner peace and wisdom.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_35.context: A man reflects on his busy life and burdens.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_36.meaning: Appreciating life's impermanence and embracing love and understanding brings spiritual growth.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_36.context: Enlightenment is achieved through love, acceptance, and embracing the present moment.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_38.meaning: Understanding that external stability relies on internal peace and education, not just religion.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_38.context: Two paths to destroy a nation: causing internal conflict or keeping people uneducated.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_40.meaning: Education and seeking truth leads to personal growth and understanding.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_40.context: A man reflects on the importance of knowledge and wisdom.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_41.meaning: Accepting the impermanence of life brings inner peace and wisdom.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_41.context: A man reflects on the transient nature of life and the importance of acceptance.

buddhism_sutras_part_52_42.meaning: Sharing knowledge and helping others brings personal growth and understanding.
buddhism_sutras_part_52_42.context: Ulenspiegel and the hospitaller discuss healing and wisdom.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_21.meaning: The story reminds us that people can be judged harshly, and we should think before condemning others.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_21.context: Pennie says they burned Joan of Arc last week, a historical event remembered in a story.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_22.meaning: It teaches that all life is connected, and we should seek understanding of the deeper source behind everything.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_22.context: The verse compares everything to a plant growing from a seed, asking how the Absolute causes all things.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_23.meaning: True happiness comes from loving others, not from having many possessions or riches.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_23.context: The verse says a happy life is measured by love, not by money or wealth.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_24.meaning: The story warns that losing control can lead to self-destruction and emotional numbness.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_24.context: A father, unable to control himself, falls onto a dead body and lies there like a dead person.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_25.meaning: Hope can keep us going even when things look bleak, and we should never give up too early.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_25.context: David looks at a ruined house, feels hope, and thinks the person inside might be alive.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_26.meaning: The verse shows how simple pleasures can bring joy to those who are struggling.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_26.context: A basket of wine and other drinks is carried down the street, heard by a poor widow.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_27.meaning: Being kind can deeply affect others, showing that small acts of compassion matter a lot.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_27.context: The speaker praises kindness as a powerful way to touch another person's heart.

buddhism_sutras_part_60_28.meaning: The verse reminds us that appearances can be deceiving, and we should look beyond first impressions.
buddhism_sutras_part_60_28.context: She opens a door and sees her lover, who looks like a devil, standing alone.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_24.meaning: Recognizing inner strength helps us stay calm. We should appreciate our own potential for peace and wisdom.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_24.context: Ananda brings water to the Buddha, who reflects on his own great spiritual power and presence.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_25.meaning: We must look honestly at ourselves. Seeing our true nature is better than hiding behind false images.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_25.context: A poetic line asking a mirror to reveal true reality or show nothing if truth is absent.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_26.meaning: Pause before reacting. This space lets you choose a calm response instead of an angry one.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_26.context: Mindfulness creates a gap between what happens and the stories we tell ourselves about those events.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_27.meaning: Ancient wisdom has lasted long. We can trust teachings that have guided people for many centuries.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_27.context: Scholar Rhys Davids notes that this text likely originated in the fifth century before Christ.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_28.meaning: Be kind to yourself. Accept your day as it was, and start fresh tomorrow with peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_28.context: A daily reminder to accept your actions, feelings, and thoughts without harsh judgment or regret.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_29.meaning: Show respect for those who taught you. Gratitude and reverence keep good memories and values alive.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_29.context: People honor the Buddha's remains with music, flowers, perfumes, and decorations made from their clothes.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_30.meaning: Desire cannot force change. True peace comes from within, not from clinging to others.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_30.context: A woman clings to a king who remains unmoved, like stone, despite her desperate and tight embrace.

buddhism_sutras_part_106_31.meaning: Good friends help us grow. Surround yourself with people who support your journey toward peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_106_31.context: Four wealthy friends from Benares were close companions of Yasa, who sought spiritual truth together.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_9.meaning: It shows that true strength comes from inner change, not just physical power or aggression.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_9.context: This story tells how a saint changed two oxen into fighting bulls to show a miracle.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_10.meaning: It teaches that doing good work and living simply both lead to the same inner peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_10.context: The text compares two different spiritual paths that people often think are completely separate things.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_12.meaning: It warns that being too tired or careless can make you lose your way in life.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_12.context: A tired traveler falls asleep during a long walk and misses the chance to turn back home.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_13.meaning: It reminds us that life is short, so we should not waste time on silly things.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_13.context: A prince sees old people and realizes that everyone eventually dies, which makes him feel very sad.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_14.meaning: It teaches that chasing fun all the time can ruin your life and lead you astray.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_14.context: The speaker warns that wanting too much pleasure is a big danger for every single person.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_15.meaning: It shows that kindness and simple care can help someone who is feeling alone or confused.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_15.context: A kind woman sees a young person who looks lost and asks if they have lost their family.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_16.meaning: It suggests that life is complex and good deeds do not always bring instant rewards.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_16.context: A person asks why good people get hurt when karma says you get what you give.

buddhism_sutras_part_108_17.meaning: It highlights the importance of listening to different viewpoints before making a final decision.
buddhism_sutras_part_108_17.context: A bailiff asks a man named Ulenspiegel what he thinks about a situation they are discussing.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_5.meaning: Use your thoughts to help you navigate life, but do not let them rule your heart or spirit completely.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_5.context: The mind is a useful tool for daily tasks but should not control your entire life or emotions.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_6.meaning: Self punishment is useless for growth. True mastery comes from inner peace, not from causing pain to yourself.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_6.context: Hurting your body does not help you gain knowledge or control your senses effectively in spiritual practice.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_7.meaning: This is just a factual note about the book source and has no spiritual lesson or moral meaning.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_7.context: This text describes the official publication details of two volumes ordered by the government for public record.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_8.meaning: Humble yourself to see reality clearly. Strip away distractions to find the true nature of existence.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_8.context: A person kneels down to look closely at the world and remove the false layers of illusion.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_9.meaning: Plans often change unexpectedly. Be ready for surprises and do not rely solely on your own schemes.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_9.context: A child waits for someone to leave so they can play a trick, but a servant arrives instead.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_10.meaning: Pay attention to what is happening around you. Sometimes observing others can bring new insights or joy.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_10.context: A girl looks out the window sadly until she hears a conversation between a nurse and another woman.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_11.meaning: Be grateful for good outcomes, but also acknowledge mistakes. Learning from errors helps us grow and improve.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_11.context: A woman expresses relief that a lost girl is found but criticizes the boy for letting her go.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_12.meaning: Accept your own hardships with grace. Do not expect others to suffer for you while you stay comfortable.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_12.context: A speaker asks someone to stay warm by the fire while they endure the harsh conditions outside.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_23.meaning: When you finish a hard task, keep moving forward with a clear mind and steady purpose toward your next goal.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_23.context: A man dressed for a long journey leaves Rome after clearing his conscience and travels to a town.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_24.meaning: True wisdom clears up confusion. When you find a reliable guide, your doubts fade and you feel free to move on.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_24.context: A follower tells a wise teacher that all their previous confusion has now been completely removed by his guidance.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_25.meaning: Deep love is shown through gentle looks and actions. It connects people without needing many words to be spoken.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_25.context: A character named Ambrose looks up at another person with eyes showing deep love and tender care for them.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_26.meaning: Questioning yourself helps you grow. It pushes your mind to find new paths and reach a deeper understanding of life.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_26.context: The text explains that asking yourself hard questions helps you find truth and frees your mind from old traps.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_27.meaning: Good work deserves recognition. When you do your duty well, others will notice and reward your effort and courage.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_27.context: A king watches his soldiers fight bravely and feels happy, so he gives them many gifts and rewards for their work.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_28.meaning: Sometimes we need to release tension. Treating things with care and affection can help us feel calm and happy again.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_28.context: A girl feels better after scolding one doll and gently petting another doll that has pretty hair and a nice face.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_29.meaning: This scene shows harsh treatment. It reminds us that cruelty and anger toward living things are never acceptable or kind.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_29.context: A man swears at a dirty dog, puts its skin in a bag, and kicks the living dog into a room.

buddhism_sutras_part_118_30.meaning: Every place has a story. Knowing where important events happened helps us connect with history and remember key moments.
buddhism_sutras_part_118_30.context: This is a short note about a specific village where the Buddha ate his final meal before passing away.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_39.meaning: This story shows how people can be so cruel that they kill others without any mercy or care.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_39.context: People are talking about a group who were killed by fire in a cruel and painful way.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_40.meaning: He enjoys seeing others afraid, but he stays serious and never laughs at their fear or panic.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_40.context: A man jumps at people to scare them, but he does not actually hurt them at all.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_41.meaning: A wise person cares for the soul, not the body, because the soul is the real part of you.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_41.context: This text explains what a truly wise person does with their body and their inner soul.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_42.meaning: The mother wants her chicks to break out of the shell and see the bright light of the world.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_42.context: A mother hen sits on her eggs and waits for her babies to hatch and come out.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_43.meaning: When you are awake, you are just human, but when you reach deep peace, you become divine.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_43.context: This verse describes how your inner self changes when you are awake versus when you are deep in peace.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_44.meaning: He feels unfairly blamed for a problem that is not his fault, and he is very angry about it.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_44.context: A king complains that people blame him for his wife not having any children with him.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_45.meaning: This place is perfect for the purpose because it has everything needed to make the visit successful.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_45.context: The speaker points out a specific bamboo grove that meets all the needed conditions for a visit.

buddhism_sutras_part_117_46.meaning: Do not let your thoughts control you, because they are only a small part of your true power.
buddhism_sutras_part_117_46.context: This line tells you that your true self is bigger and deeper than the thoughts in your head.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_17.meaning: When we feel hopeless, we often stop moving. We need to find a new way to keep going.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_17.context: The travelers are very sad and tired. They stop their oxen and rest under their wagons.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_18.meaning: Kindness grows inside us when we pay close attention. Being mindful helps our love for others bloom.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_18.context: Spring brings new flowers to the world. This season shows how nature wakes up and grows.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_20.meaning: People find God in different ways. Some want a big idea, while others just want a loving parent.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_20.context: This compares how two religions look for God. One seeks a big idea, the other seeks a father.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_21.meaning: Sometimes we get stuck in life. We must find a new direction instead of just standing still.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_21.context: Ambrose is stuck in a strange place. He cannot move forward or backward and just stares.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_22.meaning: People often disagree on the best path. We should listen to many voices to find the truth.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_22.context: Two men argue about the right path. Each claims his teacher showed the true way to God.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_23.meaning: Death brings a different kind of knowledge. Sometimes we learn the most from those who have passed on.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_23.context: A dead person answers a question about war. He says he knows it well because he is dead.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_24.meaning: Status can change how people treat you. High rank brings attention, but it does not always bring peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_24.context: This compares a group's high rank to a famous French lady. She had great power at court.

buddhism_sutras_part_121_25.meaning: Life can be harsh and painful. We must protect ourselves from the heat of the world.
buddhism_sutras_part_121_25.context: The sun is very hot and bright. It burns the head of a person named Nele.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_9.meaning: True wisdom lifts your spirit above small worries, letting you see the world with clear eyes.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_9.context: A holy person rises high like a bird, showing freedom from earthly limits.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_10.meaning: You must grow your inner peace and purity before you can truly enter the holy place.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_10.context: The sacred land is open only to people who have a deep inner spiritual heart.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_11.meaning: A good leader helps lost people find their way, showing them how to live with purpose.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_11.context: People are confused and blind, but a wise teacher guides both gods and humans.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_12.meaning: Be fully here now, speak the truth, and let your actions spread a warm feeling of love.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_12.context: Working with others means being present, honest, and kind in every single moment you share.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_13.meaning: Stop holding onto things that fade away. Do good deeds, because they last and shape your future.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_13.context: The Buddha tells the tempter that his path is hidden, then advises on how to act well.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_14.meaning: This scene shows how people often waste time on small talk and noise instead of finding peace.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_14.context: Old women sit together, knitting and gossiping loudly, making strange and unpleasant sounds around them.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_15.meaning: Thinking you are a fixed, separate self is a trap. Let go of this ego to find true freedom.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_15.context: The text discusses the belief in a permanent self, which is seen as a common human mistake.

buddhism_sutras_part_124_16.meaning: Different faiths often share similar stories and lessons, showing that truth can be found in many places.
buddhism_sutras_part_124_16.context: This line lists sources and comparisons between different religious texts, showing their shared themes.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_8.meaning: Kindness and gratitude lead to friendship. Friends help each other without distinction.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_8.context: A stork with a hurt wing is healed, and meets Claes who catches fish for her. The stork thanks Claes and they become friends.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_10.meaning: Understanding self and others through selflessness brings intricacies. Embrace change and growth.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_10.context: Exchanging self for others brings paradoxes in understanding and practice.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_11.meaning: Be genuine and respect boundaries in interactions with others.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_11.context: A man tries to impress a woman with compliments, but refrains from flirting with her.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_12.meaning: Equality and unity are essential in understanding life.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_12.context: A wise man seeks guidance and learns to see the world as one without divisions.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_13.meaning: Kindness and humility lead to prosperity and connections with those in power.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_13.context: Ulenspiegel meets the landgrave and receives help and friendship.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_14.meaning: Kindness and compassion unite all beings, regardless of status.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_14.context: No distinction is made between high and low, rich and poor, or powerful and weak.

buddhism_sutras_part_126_16.meaning: Equality and unity are essential in understanding life.
buddhism_sutras_part_126_16.context: A wise man seeks guidance and learns to see the world as one without divisions.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_29.meaning: True belonging comes from feeling accepted and treated with love, not just from living in a specific house.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_29.context: This line defines home not as a place, but as a feeling of safety and kindness.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_30.meaning: When you let go of fear and ego, you feel connected to all people instead of being isolated.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_30.context: The text describes opening the heart and lists the fears and selfish thoughts that block this openness.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_31.meaning: Our minds often create idealized images of people, which can lead to disappointment when reality differs from fantasy.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_31.context: A character named Pennie imagines a woman named Ethelwyn as perfect before she has even met her in person.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_32.meaning: Memories of the past can distract us from the present moment, showing how the mind wanders easily.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_32.context: A man named Andrew remembers a young woman named Mollie while looking at someone else named Dickie.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_33.meaning: There is a difference between actively asking for help and graciously accepting a gift that is freely offered to you.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_33.context: This text discusses legal rules about asking for money and accepting gifts from people in different states.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_34.meaning: Kindness and support from others are valuable, and we should recognize and appreciate the help we receive.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_34.context: The narrator notes that a woman had helped a man many times in the past with great effort.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_35.meaning: People often judge others harshly for having different beliefs, showing how easily we can divide ourselves over ideas.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_35.context: Two men discuss a follower of Luther, calling his beliefs a heresy against the Roman religion.

buddhism_sutras_part_131_36.meaning: Knowing the names of early followers helps us understand the history and community behind the spiritual teachings.
buddhism_sutras_part_131_36.context: This is a dictionary entry identifying a person named Punna who was a friend of the disciple Yasa.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_22.meaning: When many people act together, their voices can create a powerful, sometimes harmful, energy.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_22.context: A group of people all shouted loudly in a dangerous place.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_23.meaning: Through quiet practice, we can feel the deep beauty and sweetness of our inner spirit.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_23.context: Meditation is described as hearing, seeing, smelling, touching, and tasting inner spiritual qualities.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_24.meaning: If we accept life as it comes, we can move through it calmly and easily.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_24.context: The verse says not to judge life by limited human understanding.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_25.meaning: He practiced great patience and tolerance instead of seeking revenge or justice.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_25.context: Someone chose not to go to court or complain about wrongs he faced.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_26.meaning: What we think of as our true self is actually temporary and can change.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_26.context: The verse says that the self is not eternal or unchanging.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_27.meaning: Sometimes people mock what others value, showing a lack of respect or understanding.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_27.context: A town is proud of a royal doctor, but the people only laugh.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_28.meaning: Awareness is the base; thoughts arise within it, not the other way around.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_28.context: The verse compares thought and awareness in a simple way.

buddhism_sutras_part_136_29.meaning: He must act quickly and gather information from many places to find the truth.
buddhism_sutras_part_136_29.context: Andrew is told to leave immediately and ask questions at every house.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_3.meaning: He tries to show his foolishness loudly, but it only makes him look silly and unimportant.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_3.context: A foolish man jumps, shouts, and wants to be seen as a lowly person, using loud trumpets.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_4.meaning: Patience helps you understand what others truly want and respect their choices.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_4.context: Someone says you should wait to see what a woman prefers to be called.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_5.meaning: Seeing every part of something helps you use it wisely and appreciate its full value.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_5.context: A herb collector imagines all parts of a plant and how they can be used.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_6.meaning: Careful organization and faith in others can make difficult tasks easier and more meaningful.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_6.context: Mr. Hawthorn spends 15 minutes sorting Miss Unity’s belongings while David watches, trusting his father.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_7.meaning: A well-structured lesson makes spiritual ideas easier to learn and apply in daily life.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_7.context: The Buddha’s teachings are arranged in a clear, orderly way to help people understand them.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_8.meaning: Life’s ups and downs are natural, and we learn to move with the changing currents.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_8.context: Water waves change size and feel, driven by wind that shifts direction and strength.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_9.meaning: Forgiveness can heal old hurts and bring peace to both the giver and the receiver.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_9.context: Someone offers a promise to forgive past wrongs to a family and their relatives.

buddhism_sutras_part_139_10.meaning: Different people have different plans, and sometimes we must trust others to act for us.
buddhism_sutras_part_139_10.context: A person says you will never see him, but another says he will talk to him.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_9.meaning: Find peace by simplifying your life. Let go of mental noise and connect with the natural world.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_9.context: Nature brings calm. Clear your mind of clutter to find inner peace and quiet joy.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_10.meaning: Think for yourself. Do not just accept feelings taught by others. Create your own true emotional responses.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_10.context: Schools teach us what to feel. We do not learn to create our own emotions naturally.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_11.meaning: Keep going when tired. Your strength helps others. Do not give up because your effort matters greatly.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_11.context: The Buddha felt weak. He kept walking to stay awake and save his followers from despair.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_12.meaning: Pause to reflect. Check your progress. Understand what your hard work and discipline have truly achieved for you.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_12.context: He sat under a tree. He checked his mind and reviewed the results of his hard work.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_13.meaning: Be still to see clearly. Deep truths appear only when you stop rushing and listen to silence.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_13.context: Quietness reveals hidden truths. You cannot see deep things when your mind is busy and loud.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_14.meaning: True insight connects us. It removes barriers and helps us understand the deeper truth of life.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_14.context: Enlightenment lifts the veil. It bridges the gap between our world and deeper spiritual reality.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_15.meaning: Help those ready to change. Giving to unprepared minds yields no good results or growth.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_15.context: Giving to those controlled by bad habits is like planting seeds in poor soil.

buddhism_sutras_part_142_16.meaning: Simple acts show love. Preparing food with care is a way to honor and serve others.
buddhism_sutras_part_142_16.context: Chunda cooked rice cakes and meat. He prepared a meal for the Buddha with great care.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_20.meaning: When you focus your mind on truth, you break free from fear and desire that hold you back.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_20.context: People who think deeply and follow the right path find freedom from bad habits and mental traps.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_21.meaning: Being aware helps us feel connected to everything in nature, showing that we are part of one whole.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_21.context: Paying close attention helps us see how we are linked to nature and the world around us.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_22.meaning: Distance can create separation, reminding us that gaps in understanding or relationship need to be bridged with care.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_22.context: Two groups moved away from each other, creating a large empty space between them in the story.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_23.meaning: Names are just words. The real value of something comes from its essence, not what we call it.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_23.context: Labels do not change the true nature of things, just as a flower smells good regardless of its name.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_24.meaning: Wandering without purpose leads to confusion. We need a clear goal to find peace and direction in life.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_24.context: A person wanders without a clear direction, and others wonder where he has gone or what he is doing.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_25.meaning: Excessive celebration can weaken our balance. We should enjoy life but keep our mind clear and steady.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_25.context: A leader sees someone standing unsteadily at a party, smiling but looking weak or perhaps intoxicated by joy.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_26.meaning: Silence shows respect for wisdom. We learn best when we stop our own noise and listen with an open heart.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_26.context: When a wise teacher enters a room, everyone stops talking quietly to show respect and prepare to listen.

buddhism_sutras_part_144_27.meaning: Let your inner light shine. Do not hide your goodness or wisdom, but share it openly with the world.
buddhism_sutras_part_144_27.context: A speaker encourages someone to emerge from darkness like the moon appearing from behind clouds to shine brightly.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_20.meaning: Your mind is the main battlefield. You must control your thoughts to handle external difficulties with calm and strength.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_20.context: This verse describes the internal struggle where your thoughts fight against outside pressures and challenges.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_21.meaning: Breathing with full attention brings life energy. Mindless breathing is just air. Awareness turns simple breath into spiritual power.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_21.context: This text contrasts simple breathing with mindful breathing, highlighting the difference between automatic action and conscious awareness.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_22.meaning: True modesty comes from doing your duty. When you pay your dues, you act with humility and respect for others.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_22.context: People sit modestly and dress simply because they feel they are fulfilling their duties and paying their social debts.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_23.meaning: Do not judge by appearances alone. Look deeper to understand the truth. Surprise often hides the real nature of a situation.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_23.context: Onlookers were shocked and looked around the garden to see if the woman was actually there or not.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_24.meaning: Find joy in simple, grounded places. You do not need high status. Happiness comes from appreciating your current humble surroundings.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_24.context: A man lived happily in the kitchen and cellar, leaving the attic space for the cats to use.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_25.meaning: Distance helps you see clearly. Stepping back from daily routines allows you to understand your life from a wider, calmer viewpoint.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_25.context: Moving away from objects gives a new view. Traveling to new places offers a fresh perspective on your own life.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_26.meaning: Opportunities can bring fear. Do not rush into new experiences. Understand your feelings before accepting exciting but scary changes.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_26.context: A boy was told he would ride a fast horse, but he cried because he was afraid or sad.

buddhism_sutras_part_146_27.meaning: Success comes from good deeds. Do kind things every day. Your positive actions create the foundation for your future happiness and achievements.
buddhism_sutras_part_146_27.context: A person attributes their success to good karma, suggesting that positive actions in the past led to current rewards.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_7.meaning: Simple daily tasks and humble routines can bring peace and contentment to your life if you focus on them.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_7.context: Miss Unity buys simple food items at the market and carries them home in a basket.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_8.meaning: True humanity comes from compassion and connection with others, not from selfish desires or prideful attitudes.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_8.context: This verse suggests that letting go of ego and self-centered thoughts leads to a deeper sense of humanity.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_9.meaning: Holding onto anger hurts your own peace and health, so you should release negative emotions to protect your well-being.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_9.context: Anger is described as a force that harms the person feeling it, rather than just the target of the anger.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_10.meaning: Kindness and good deeds naturally lead to positive outcomes and happiness in your life and for others.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_10.context: Good actions performed with a pure heart are said to bring positive results and blessings to the doer.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_11.meaning: Solitude and quiet reflection are valuable for restoring energy and finding inner peace after social engagements.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_11.context: After social interactions, Miss Unity returns to her quiet home and spends the evening alone in peace.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_12.meaning: Knowledge is useless if not applied to daily life, so you must practice what you learn to truly benefit.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_12.context: Reciting scriptures without understanding or practicing their teachings is compared to counting cattle that do not belong to you.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_13.meaning: Helping others who are in need is a way to honor the kindness you have received in your own life.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_13.context: The verse encourages remembering those who helped you and paying that kindness forward to others who are struggling.

buddhism_sutras_part_149_14.meaning: Try to understand another person's perspective and experiences before judging their actions or decisions in life.
buddhism_sutras_part_149_14.context: The verse uses the metaphor of walking in another person's shoes to encourage empathy before making judgments about others.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_31.meaning: Touching a wise person helps you see the good inside yourself and understand your own true nature.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_31.context: Meeting a true teacher connects you to their deep wisdom and your own inner potential.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_32.meaning: Your thoughts build your character. If you control your mind, you control your life and your happiness.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_32.context: The Buddha taught that our minds create our reality and shape who we truly are.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_33.meaning: Small moments pass quickly. We should notice the tiny details of life before they disappear.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_33.context: A woman leaves a room just as a small insect finishes its short flight path.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_34.meaning: Even when we feel great, we worry about losing it. We must learn to be calm and present.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_34.context: Life has happy times and hard times, but fear often hides behind our moments of joy.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_35.meaning: We must be kind to all living things. Hurting the helpless shows a lack of compassion and love.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_35.context: Hurting weak animals who cannot defend themselves is considered the most terrible kind of violence.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_36.meaning: Hard times teach us to appreciate good times. Seeing this balance brings peace and deep joy.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_36.context: Where there is great pain, there is also great happiness if you look closely enough.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_37.meaning: Silence can be powerful. Sometimes not speaking shows deep thought or a calm inner state.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_37.context: A woman asks a quiet boy why he speaks so little, but he does not answer her.

buddhism_sutras_part_150_38.meaning: Stop believing every thought is true. Watch your thoughts pass by to find peace and freedom.
buddhism_sutras_part_150_38.context: We suffer because we think our thoughts are us instead of just passing mental events.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_9.meaning: True legacy comes from sharing kindness and love, not from money or status, inspiring others to be good.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_9.context: A wise teacher speaks about leaving behind material wealth to share stories of love and kindness with others.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_10.meaning: Violence and weapons cause harm, reminding us that peace and non-harm are better paths for spiritual growth.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_10.context: A list of weapons is mentioned, describing the tools of war and conflict used by groups in history.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_11.meaning: Nature can be a place of peace and wisdom, helping us find inner calm and spiritual awakening.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_11.context: The sacred tree where the Buddha sat to find enlightenment is identified as a specific type of fig tree.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_12.meaning: Some truths are personal and deep, requiring inner reflection rather than public display to be truly understood.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_12.context: The Buddha explains that some things like love and deep wisdom are kept secret or private from the public.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_13.meaning: Life moves at different speeds for everyone, so we should focus on our own journey and present moment.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_13.context: A long procession is described where candles burn down at different rates, showing the passage of time and distance.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_14.meaning: Different beliefs may lead to similar peace, encouraging respect for diverse spiritual journeys and shared human values.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_14.context: A question is asked about whether all spiritual paths lead to the same ultimate goal of union with the divine.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_15.meaning: Focus on living well today, as the present moment is the only time we truly have to shape our lives.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_15.context: A poem reflects on how living well today turns the past into happy memories and the future into hope.

buddhism_sutras_part_156_16.meaning: Community support and safety are important, reminding us to care for each other and protect the vulnerable among us.
buddhism_sutras_part_156_16.context: A question is raised about whether a woman could safely travel alone into a village, highlighting concerns about safety.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_31.meaning: Unexpected noises can surprise us, reminding us to stay alert and open to new experiences.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_31.context: Ulenspiegel hears hammering at night, wondering if he will wake up to the sound.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_32.meaning: Observing nature teaches us to notice what is missing and to appreciate what we have.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_32.context: He sees a quiet horse-chestnut tree and wonders why there are no flowering trees nearby.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_33.meaning: Offering simple kindness to those we respect can create positive connections.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_33.context: If you meet Buddha in a lane, you should give him a ball to play with.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_34.meaning: Comparing similar ideas helps us understand deeper meanings across different teachings.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_34.context: The text lists parallelisms, referencing Gospel VII and source BSt, page number.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_35.meaning: New thoughts lead to new actions, which shape a different tomorrow.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_35.context: To change your future, you must change your thoughts and beliefs today.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_36.meaning: True insight requires patience and clear, focused effort, not hurried or chaotic attempts.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_36.context: Few find enlightenment quickly; no one discovers it through nonsense or confusion.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_37.meaning: Our identity is made of many elements, and understanding each helps us grow.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_37.context: Individuality is described as a mix of many parts, like a spinning wheel.

buddhism_sutras_part_184_38.meaning: People often rush, but knowing where you are headed gives purpose to your journey.
buddhism_sutras_part_184_38.context: A traveling salesman asks Ulenspiegel why he is in such a hurry, and he replies he is going home.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_34.meaning: If a belief reaches people, it does not automatically change their actions or character.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_34.context: A teaching about how a certain idea spreads but does not change people.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_35.meaning: Continuing to see a separate self leads to pain, old age, illness, and eventual death.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_35.context: Explains that new lives of self cause suffering, aging, sickness, and death.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_36.meaning: When the ego disappears, one is free from cravings and remains pure, unaffected by desires.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_36.context: Describes a person whose self is gone, free from desire and unspoiled by wants.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_37.meaning: You must first accept who you are to consciously change and improve yourself.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_37.context: Stresses the need to accept oneself before making deliberate changes.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_38.meaning: The speaker returns to a spot, and someone asks why they should stop there.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_38.context: A narrative fragment about returning to a place and a question about stopping.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_39.meaning: The text cites similar passages and notes the source for further study.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_39.context: Mentions parallel verses and source references in a scholarly note.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_40.meaning: Pray to the universe to help yourself and guide others to help themselves.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_40.context: Suggests a daily prayer asking the universe for self-help and helping others.

buddhism_sutras_part_198_41.meaning: Being enthusiastic gains knowledge; being indifferent causes knowledge to fade away.
buddhism_sutras_part_198_41.context: States that zeal brings knowledge, while lack of zeal causes loss of knowledge.

buddhism_zen_part_1_32.meaning: We should value each moment, knowing it is unique and will not repeat.
buddhism_zen_part_1_32.context: Life is precious because it is short and never comes back the same way.

buddhism_zen_part_1_33.meaning: Focus on now, because the past is gone and the future is not yet here.
buddhism_zen_part_1_33.context: There is no real destination; we only exist in the present moment.

buddhism_zen_part_1_34.meaning: Learn to let go of false feelings and accept what really is.
buddhism_zen_part_1_34.context: Balance comes when we stop reacting to harmful emotions and see true reality.

buddhism_zen_part_1_35.meaning: Realize that the goal is inside you, not somewhere else outside.
buddhism_zen_part_1_35.context: He thinks what he needs is far away, but it is right beside him.

buddhism_zen_part_1_36.meaning: Act now to help others instead of delaying or hoping someone else will.
buddhism_zen_part_1_36.context: Do not wait for someone else to act; help immediately when you see need.

buddhism_zen_part_1_37.meaning: Adjust your thoughts and the world will shift to match your new view.
buddhism_zen_part_1_37.context: Changing how we see things changes everything around us.

buddhism_zen_part_1_38.meaning: Decide if thinking helps or hinders your peace and clarity.
buddhism_zen_part_1_38.context: The real question is whether we should think or not think.

buddhism_zen_part_1_39.meaning: Use your feelings to guide changes that bring you closer to your desired life.
buddhism_zen_part_1_39.context: Feel good and keep moving toward your reality; if not, rethink your beliefs.

buddhism_zen_part_8_47.meaning: Peace comes when we stop chasing things and simply notice the small gifts that arrive on their own.
buddhism_zen_part_8_47.context: A quiet night scene where the smell of flowers drifts in from a distant garden.

buddhism_zen_part_8_48.meaning: We must look closely at who we really are to find peace instead of fighting against our own nature.
buddhism_zen_part_8_48.context: A deep question about whether our physical self and our thoughts are truly separate or one thing.

buddhism_zen_part_8_49.meaning: Approach every new moment with fresh curiosity and joy, treating each experience like a beautiful flower waiting to be enjoyed.
buddhism_zen_part_8_49.context: Life presents many different moments and challenges that we face every single day without fail.

buddhism_zen_part_8_50.meaning: Stop trying to fill your inner void with external things and learn to be happy with what you already have.
buddhism_zen_part_8_50.context: People often feel empty inside because they are never satisfied with their current lives or possessions.

buddhism_zen_part_9_1.meaning: Focus on something lovely each day so that creative inspiration can flow into your life naturally and easily.
buddhism_zen_part_9_1.context: A daily practice of finding beauty in ordinary things to open your heart to new ideas.

buddhism_zen_part_9_2.meaning: Make your own joy the top priority every morning, because a happy heart makes all other tasks much easier.
buddhism_zen_part_9_2.context: A mother tells her child that happiness is the most important goal for the day.

buddhism_zen_part_9_3.meaning: True goodness stands alone without needing an enemy, so let your kindness be pure and not based on opposition.
buddhism_zen_part_9_3.context: When your definition of good depends on hating something else, it is not truly good at all.

buddhism_zen_part_9_4.meaning: We should appreciate what we have now instead of craving what is scarce, because true value lies in presence.
buddhism_zen_part_9_4.context: Humans often value things the most when they are rare or when they cannot enjoy them fully.

buddhism_zen_part_10_12.meaning: Understand and accept love naturally, as it leads to personal growth. Trying to control or suppress it is futile. Embrace life's journey.
buddhism_zen_part_10_12.context: We visited a monastery where the wise Chan master Yun-men taught Zen philosophy. His famous quote about love highlights the importance of freedom and growth.

buddhism_zen_part_10_13.meaning: Observe and accept your emotions without judgment. Recognize that our consciousness unites us all.
buddhism_zen_part_10_13.context: Zen master Yun-men's teaching on emotional healing and interconnectedness.

buddhism_zen_part_10_14.meaning: Zen is about living a question rather than seeking answers. Embrace uncertainty and inner wisdom.
buddhism_zen_part_10_14.context: Zen master Enso Roshi discusses the essence of Zen philosophy.

buddhism_zen_part_10_15.meaning: Fanaticism in religion or beliefs can lead to losing faith. Keep an open mind and grow through personal experiences.
buddhism_zen_part_10_15.context: Zen master Yun-men warns against religious fanaticism.

buddhism_zen_part_10_16.meaning: Engaging in emotions and actions intensifies them. Be mindful of your choices.
buddhism_zen_part_10_16.context: Zen master Yun-men explains the power of emotions and actions.

buddhism_zen_part_10_17.meaning: Understand that reality is subjective and constantly changing. Embrace the journey of life.
buddhism_zen_part_10_17.context: Zen master Yun-men's teaching on the nature of reality.

buddhism_zen_part_10_18.meaning: Zen is about finding inner peace and wisdom through questioning and understanding.
buddhism_zen_part_10_18.context: Zen master Enso Roshi discusses the essence of Zen philosophy.

buddhism_zen_part_10_19.meaning: Understand that reality is subjective and constantly changing. Embrace the journey of life.
buddhism_zen_part_10_19.context: Zen master Yun-men's teaching on the nature of reality.

buddhism_zen_part_11_19.meaning: You must quiet your own mind to hear the truth, because external shouting cannot reach the deep silence within your soul.
buddhism_zen_part_11_19.context: Zen teaches that true silence is not just the absence of noise but a deep inner state of peace.

buddhism_zen_part_11_20.meaning: Accept your mistakes as teachers, because they show you where you need to grow and help you find your true path.
buddhism_zen_part_11_20.context: This verse suggests that our flaws and mistakes are not failures but essential tools for learning and growing spiritually.

buddhism_zen_part_11_21.meaning: Stop worrying about yesterday or tomorrow, because the only time you can actually live and change things is right now.
buddhism_zen_part_11_21.context: The text explains that time is a mental construct, and only the current moment is truly real and tangible.

buddhism_zen_part_11_22.meaning: True holiness is not a place you visit, but a feeling of peace that arises from within your own heart and mind.
buddhism_zen_part_11_22.context: A spiritual experience is described where the physical world transforms into a sacred space within the person's heart.

buddhism_zen_part_11_23.meaning: Step back from your rigid thoughts, because the answer you seek is often hidden just outside the narrow box of your mind.
buddhism_zen_part_11_23.context: The passage warns that we often miss solutions because we look too narrowly, trapped by our own limited ways of thinking.

buddhism_zen_part_11_25.meaning: Let go of your need for praise and status, so you can see your true self without the mask of vanity and pride.
buddhism_zen_part_11_25.context: The text describes removing the false pride of the ego to reveal the true, unadorned nature of who you really are.

buddhism_zen_part_11_26.meaning: Your mind creates your reality, so changing your inner thoughts and feelings will directly change the world you experience around you.
buddhism_zen_part_11_26.context: This teaching explains that the world we see is not separate from us, but is shaped by our own awareness.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_32.meaning: We all make big errors, but admitting them is the first step toward true healing.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_32.context: A character expresses deep regret for their past mistakes while Anna listens with worry.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_33.meaning: Sometimes we must move slowly and carefully when we are tired or feeling weak.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_33.context: A woman climbs the stairs slowly, holding the railing for support as she goes up.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_34.meaning: Having a safe and comfortable place to rest helps us feel secure and at peace.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_34.context: The story describes the bedrooms as the biggest and most comfortable rooms in the entire house.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_35.meaning: We often feel relieved and happy when a loved one returns to our side.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_35.context: A tired person asks if the father is home, and the girl looks up in surprise.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_36.meaning: Our inner happiness grows naturally when we are fed by love, light, and care.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_36.context: The text compares a person's joy to a tree growing from the earth with sun and rain.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_37.meaning: True kindness comes from the heart, not from seeking praise or recognition from others.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_37.context: Anna helps nurses care for a sick woman, working hard even though others do not care.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_38.meaning: We are all connected to the whole world and share its beauty and resources together.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_38.context: The passage describes a person owning the wide earth, including cities, fields, and rivers.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_39.meaning: Fear feels much bigger when we are alone, but we must stay brave and keep hope.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_39.context: A cold girl stands alone in a hallway, watching her candle flame flicker in the wind.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_40.meaning: We often miss the deeper spiritual meaning behind simple things because we only see their surface value.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_40.context: A woman sees a simple object and thinks it is just a cheap item for daily use.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_41.meaning: Sometimes things that look normal on the outside can feel wrong or unpleasant when you actually try to use them.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_41.context: A person looks at a plate of damp bread with many seeds and finds it impossible to eat.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_42.meaning: We often face our own fears alone and keep our closest loved ones out of our personal struggles.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_42.context: A woman likes to imagine hard tests for herself but never brings her partner along on these trips.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_43.meaning: Family love is a strong force that pulls us back to the people who care about us most.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_43.context: A mother reads a letter from her son who is desperate to see her again soon.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_44.meaning: Sometimes a small change in perspective or a new view can turn a complaint into a moment of comfort.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_44.context: A woman complains about the cold, and her husband opens a door to show a warm dinner table.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_45.meaning: It is wise to act quickly to fix small problems before they grow into much bigger and harder issues.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_45.context: One person suggests fixing a problem right away, and the other person agrees that this is the right thing.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_46.meaning: Taking a moment to enjoy nature can help you feel calm and refreshed after a long period of stress.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_46.context: A woman leans out of a window and breathes in the warm air of a sunny spring day.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_47.meaning: True happiness is not just about your own feelings, but it also depends on how you treat others.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_1_47.context: Two people discuss how trying to be happy for yourself does not always make everyone around you happy.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_17.meaning: Guilt can make us reject good things, showing how inner pain affects our daily actions and choices.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_17.context: A woman feels deep shame and fear while eating, so she stops and pushes her food away.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_18.meaning: True kindness allows others to choose their own path, respecting their freedom and personal dignity.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_18.context: A man asks if he should keep a lady, and the other agrees she can stay if she wishes.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_19.meaning: We often miss how others view our actions, leading to misunderstandings about fairness and value.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_19.context: She never thought about how he saw his gift as fair payment for what he gave.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_20.meaning: When we are overwhelmed, we may stop engaging with life, drifting through days without true presence.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_20.context: She stopped thinking deeply and just let life happen to her, doing tasks without real awareness.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_21.meaning: Contentment comes when we stop wanting more and accept what is enough, finding joy in simplicity.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_21.context: She decided to accept simple things because others seemed happy with them, so she found peace too.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_22.meaning: Leaders should serve with humility, not pride, ensuring their focus is on the message, not themselves.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_22.context: The pastor stands proudly before the altar, his chest rising above the gold edge of his Bible.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_23.meaning: In hard times, we must drop our masks and face the truth, because only honesty helps us heal.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_23.context: In a sad place, both people dropped all fake pretenses and kept only what was truly real.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_24.meaning: Life can turn beautiful things into mess, reminding us that purity is hard to keep in a rough world.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_17_24.context: Outside, rain slowly turned the thick street dust into a dark, wet layer of dirty sludge.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_7.meaning: We often feel hurt when loved ones do not include us in their important relationships.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_7.context: A woman feels ignored because her partner is slow to share his social life with her.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_8.meaning: Old places can become wild and messy, showing how time changes even strong structures.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_8.context: An old, deep ditch is filled with wild grass, bushes, and broken pieces of stone.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_9.meaning: Sudden bad news can wake us up and force us to deal with serious problems.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_9.context: A boss sends a late night message about a violent fight between workers over a woman.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_10.meaning: Clear markers help us understand tricky parts of a story without getting confused or lost.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_10.context: The text notes that certain difficult words are marked with lines under them for readers.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_11.meaning: Sometimes we need to ask for help or share information to understand what is happening.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_11.context: One person says they cannot read the notes, so the other person asks to see them.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_12.meaning: We often realize too late that we should have valued the people who loved us most.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_12.context: A woman regrets not spending enough time with her husband before he died or changed.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_13.meaning: Sometimes we shut out the world to protect our feelings or escape from pain.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_13.context: A man sits against a wall, ignoring the noise around him and not listening to footsteps.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_14.meaning: Clear thinking helps us see hidden motives and understand why people act the way they do.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_18_14.context: A woman suddenly understands that a girl planned this situation to gain power and control.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_22_49.meaning: Sometimes we must accept reality instead of fighting it, because some things are beyond our control.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_22_49.context: A woman realizes her situation is fixed and cannot be changed by her own efforts.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_22_50.meaning: Do not waste energy on impossible tasks, because nature has clear limits on what can happen.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_22_50.context: A speaker uses a wild animal example to show that some things are impossible to do.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_1.meaning: Sometimes good advice feels useless if the person is too stubborn or the situation is hopeless.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_1.context: A man laughs because he knows his warning to a friend will not actually help.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_2.meaning: Power and authority often flow from the top down, requiring others to listen and obey.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_2.context: A strong messenger delivers a royal command to a smaller, weaker archer in the story.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_3.meaning: Sometimes you must leave a place if your skills do not fit the needs of the people.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_3.context: A woman leaves a busy home because she cannot comfort a sad mother there.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_4.meaning: It feels good when your thoughtful choices are appreciated and understood by the people you care about.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_4.context: Anna is happy that her friend immediately likes the special book she carefully picked out.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_5.meaning: Physical weakness can make life harder, reminding us that our bodies are not always strong.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_5.context: The narrator describes two characters who are very thin and lack physical strength or health.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_6.meaning: Nature can be overwhelming and intense, showing how alive and active the world truly is.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_23_6.context: The scene describes a hot, smelly afternoon filled with flowers and buzzing bees everywhere.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_20.meaning: Sometimes people get tired of being told what they should do, so they shut down the conversation.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_20.context: A character angrily tells another person to stop complaining about their moral duties to others.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_21.meaning: This shows the basic, simple setup of a prison cell where a prisoner eats his meals.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_21.context: A guard points to a small shelf where a prisoner keeps his food and drink items.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_22.meaning: The harsh weather reflects a tense or uncomfortable mood, making the setting feel heavy and difficult.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_22.context: The scene describes a hot, dry garden where trees move in the wind and the sun shines hard.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_23.meaning: It shows how practical and cheap living can be in some places, making small expenses easy to handle.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_23.context: A woman needs new clothes because she has grown, but she can buy them very cheaply in Germany.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_24.meaning: This reveals her inner doubt and curiosity about whether a relationship was truly caring and affectionate.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_24.context: A woman whispers a quiet question to herself, wondering if a past moment was full of deep love.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_25.meaning: It shows a desire to be considerate and respectful by keeping a distance to protect someone else.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_25.context: A person thinks about staying in a specific town to avoid bothering or annoying another woman.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_26.meaning: This moment captures the sudden danger and fear that comes when an animal is caught unexpectedly.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_26.context: A deer goes down to a water source at night and gets trapped in a hunter's snare.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_27.meaning: It highlights how surprisingly cheap the land is, making the cost seem almost unbelievable to the speaker.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_26_27.context: Someone expresses shock at the idea of spending even a tiny amount of money to buy land here.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_28_32.meaning: This verse talks about being mindful of when and how to share one's beliefs. It highlights the importance of considering the situation and the impact on others before preaching. Doubt is healthy as it helps us think critically and choose the right time and place for sharing our thoughts.
buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_28_32.context: A character named Peyton is questioning the idea of preaching at all times and situations. They express doubt about the necessity of always sharing their beliefs.

buddhism_jatakas_&_legends_part_28_33.meaning: This verse discusses the consequences of our actions and the importance of being cautious. It reminds us that our choices have ramifications and we should think before we act.
